desc: Formalize the reduction: define prefix-sum variables P_0..P_{N-1}, derive per-person constraints (P at interior towns ≥ 1 relative to endpoints, endpoints equal), and prove feasibility ⟺ no contradictory pair of constraints; identify exactly which pairs of people conflict (nested/crossing interval conditions with orientation).

Validate the proposed bad-pair predicate with a brute-force difference-constraints checker on tiny cases, and complete the proof of the pairwise/Helly lemma (no bad pair ⇒ construct potentials by laminar depth; bad pair ⇒ positive cycle).

Complete the rigorous Helly/pairwise proof: no bad pair ⇒ laminar family, assign potentials by depth with enough integer slack for alternating orientations; bad pair ⇒ exhibit a two-variable positive cycle.

Design the `prevBad[i]` computation: handle shared-endpoint cases with coordinate maps (`same left`, `same right`, `same unordered interval`) taking max previous index; handle same-orientation proper crossings via offline sweeps/segment trees keyed by endpoints, avoiding pair enumeration; prove the geometric candidate set for the max-index previous conflict is sufficient.
Implement shared-endpoint candidate maps and integrate into `prevBad`.
Implement the same-orientation crossing max-previous computation via offline sweep/CDQ with compressed town coordinates; verify against the exact `O(M^2)` path on random small/medium tests.
Replace the large-`M` placeholder with sparse-table/segment-tree RMQ over `prevBad` and answer all queries.
Write the full Python solution with fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer), careful 0/1-indexing, and verify logic against the provided samples mentally (not by execution).

Edge-case audit: confirm handling of reversed travel direction (S_i > T_i), minimal-length paths (|S-T|=2), and duplicate-free guarantee usage; stress reasoning on small N by brute-force LP check conceptually.
Stress test full solution against brute force on random small cases before finalizing.
